subject: Finly discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finly.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.k@finly.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T14:05:00Z
Subject: Finly discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements
Attachments: finly-discovery-notes.pdf

Hi Samir / Aisha,

Thanks again for the call earlier â€” appreciate the time. Below is a short recap so we have alignment on pain, current stack, success criteria, and the immediate next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

1) Pain points / impact
- Users see intermittent slow responses during peak usage; current p95 for single-turn generation is ~460ms which hurts conversion for the new live-chat feature.
- Streaming experience is inconsistent: initial token often delayed (perceived slowness) and some sessions drop mid-stream when concurrency rises.
- Cost and predictability: high bill variability with current vendor; they want predictable unit economics for budgeting.

2) Current stack / constraints
- Prod uses ManagedAPI (third-party) + an internal router for multi-tenant traffic.
- Typical request: 1-3 prompts per session, average response length ~120 tokens, spikes to 350 tokens on longer flows.
- Peak concurrent sessions estimated at 250-350; sustained concurrency during peak window ~180.

3) Success criteria (what Finly needs to call this solved)
- p95 single-turn latency <= 250ms for standard prompts (120 tokens avg).
- Initial token latency for streaming UX < 150ms; subsequent tokens streamed steadily with minimal jitter.
- Support 300 concurrent streaming sessions with graceful degradation and predictable cost.
- No regression in output quality compared to current vendor.

4) Immediate next steps / asks from Finly
- Share representative prompt set and 24-hour traffic profile (sample CSV).
- Confirm preferred time for a short POC kickoff (aiming to run a smoke load test).
- Provide access to a non-prod API key or allow us to demo against a small traffic window.

5) Redwood proposed next steps
- We will draft a POC plan (benchmarks: single-turn p95, streaming initial token, concurrent streaming throughput) and a target test harness.
- Deliver a performance plan and estimated cost for hosted vs dedicated options.
- Share SOC2 summary and standard security docs (we can send the full pack on request).

I'll follow up with the POC plan by end of day tomorrow. Proposed follow-up: 2026-03-25 10:00 AM PT for a 30-minute POC kickoff.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Samir Patel <samir@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@finly.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T14:57:00Z
Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements
Attachments: p95-latency-snapshot.png

Thanks Marissa â€” helpful summary. A few clarifications and immediate questions: 

- The p95 number I called out (~460ms) was based on last week's production runs; happy to share the query traces. I'm attaching a latency snapshot that shows the tail spikes around 8:30 PM UTC.
- For the streaming UX: initial token latency is the biggest UX blocker. If we can get that under 150ms we consider the experience acceptable.
- On concurrency: 300 concurrent streams is our high-water mark. We expect sustained 150-200 during business hours and short spikes to 300.

Two asks for Redwood before the POC kickoff:
1) Can you outline the exact benchmark steps you plan to run for streaming? We want to understand what 'pass' looks like.
2) Any limits on prompt length or token caps we should be aware of during the POC?

I attached the snapshot. Thanks â€” we can take the 3/25 slot if that works.

Samir
Head of Product, Finly
samir@finly.com

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@finly.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements

Adding a couple more success criteria from the product team perspective: 
- Maximum jitter between token chunks should not exceed 80ms on average.
- When concurrency exceeds the target, we want graceful degradation (e.g., fallback to shorter responses or queued responses) rather than errors.
- For cost modeling, please include an estimated per-session token cost at 150 tokens/session.

Also confirming sample prompts will include a mix of short 20-40 token queries and longer 300+-token generation flows.

Thanks,
Aisha
PM, Finly

-----

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finly.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha.k@finly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements
Attachments: mvp-reqs.xlsx

Hi Samir / Aisha â€” thanks for the notes and the snapshot. Quick response from the Redwood solutions team with what we'll run for the POC and a couple of clarifying questions.

Planned POC benchmark steps (high level)
- Baseline single-turn: run 1k concurrent single-turn requests at representative prompt distribution; measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
- Streaming initial token test: run N parallel streaming sessions but only request first token to measure initial token latency distribution.
- Streaming throughput: ramp to 300 concurrent streaming sessions with representative payloads; measure sustained token-per-second throughput, jitter, and error rate.
- Degradation scenarios: simulate resource saturation to validate graceful degradation policies and fallbacks.

Clarifying questions for Finly (please reply inline)
- For streaming sessions, do you expect end-to-end SDK/WebSocket behavior or will you accept a proxied HTTP chunked stream?
- Can you provide 3-5 representative long-form prompts (we'll avoid any PHI or sensitive info)?
- Preferred traffic shape for the ramp: linear over 5 minutes or step-ramp? Our suggested default is a 3-minute linear ramp to peak.

Deliverables before kickoff
- POC plan + test harness instructions (by 2026-03-19 EOD).
- Initial performance run results and a short write-up with actionable tuning knobs (within 48 hours of test).
- Hosted vs Dedicated cost estimate & a rough timeline for Dedicated capacity if chosen.

I've attached a simple MVP requirements sheet and will send the SOC2 summary in a separate email. Confirming 2026-03-25 10:00 AM PT works for our team.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
